cards.title: Constraints Spark Innovation
cards.insight: Creative breakthroughs often emerge not from unlimited resources but from working within boundaries. When creators face limits—time, budget, tools—they're forced to find novel solutions and combinations they wouldn't otherwise consider. The friction creates focus.
cards.takeaway: Next time you face a limitation, reframe it as a creative catalyst rather than an obstacle; set one intentional constraint on a project and observe what unexpected directions emerge.

cards.title: Recombination Over Invention
cards.insight: True novelty rarely comes from creating something entirely new; instead, creativity flourishes when you combine existing ideas in unexpected ways. A musician sampling a classical piece, an architect blending styles, or a chef fusing cuisines all succeed by seeing fresh connections between disparate elements.
cards.takeaway: Practice cross-pollination: expose yourself to fields unrelated to your work and actively seek unexpected intersections between ideas from different domains.

cards.title: Iteration Beats Perfection
cards.insight: Creative work improves through repetition and feedback loops, not through waiting for perfect inspiration. Each attempt, even failed ones, teaches something and moves closer to the solution. Perfectionism often blocks the messier, richer process of discovery.
cards.takeaway: Adopt a 'ship it' mindset: commit to creating multiple rough versions quickly rather than polishing one version endlessly.

cards.title: Diverse Perspectives Multiply Possibilities
cards.insight: Homogeneous teams produce narrower solutions because everyone shares similar mental models and assumptions. When diverse backgrounds, experiences, and viewpoints collide in a creative space, the number of possible directions multiplies exponentially.
cards.takeaway: Deliberately seek collaborators or feedback from people with different expertise, cultures, or lived experiences than your own for your next creative challenge.
